title: Studying Parasitoid-Induced Long-Term Effects in Drosophila
author: Sadanandappa, Bosco

steps.title: Prepare fly culture medium
steps.instruction: Make 1 L of standard cornmeal‑molasses‑yeast medium using the reagents in Table 1: 10 g agar (1 %), 76 g molasses (7.6 %), 76 g cornmeal (7.6 %), 5 g yeast (5 %), 2 mL propionic acid (0.2 %), 4 mL NIPAGIN (0.4 %); add the dry mixture to warm water, stir and bring to a boil, then cool to 60 °C before adding propionic acid and NIPAGIN. Immediately dispense the food into narrow vials or plastic bottles, cover with sterile cheesecloth and let solidify overnight at room temperature (22‑25 °C). Store the solidified food at 18 °C for up to a week or at 4 °C for up to a month.

substeps.instruction: Add the dry reagent mixture to warm water and stir to boil.
Cool the medium to 60 °C, then add propionic acid and NIPAGIN.
Dispense food into narrow vials or plastic bottles.
Cover with sterile cheesecloth; let solidify overnight at 22‑25 °C.
Store at 18 °C for one week or at 4 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Anesthetize D. virilis and set up parental vial
steps.instruction: CO₂‑anesthetize a bottle of D. virilis, place the bottle on a fly pad, add ~20 active yeast granules to a fresh food vial, then transfer 10 female and 5 male flies (using a size 4/0 or 3/0 paintbrush) into the vial and leave the vial on its side until the flies recover (≈1‑2 min). Ensure the food medium is at room temperature and remove any condensed water with Kimwipes before adding flies. Allow the parental flies to lay eggs for 4‑5 days at room temperature, using 3‑20‑day‑old mated females for optimal laying.

substeps.instruction: Add ~20 active yeast granules to a fresh food vial.
Transfer 10 female and 5 male D. virilis into the vial with a paintbrush.
Leave the vial on its side until flies recover (≈1‑2 min).
Confirm the food medium is at room temperature; remove condensation with Kimwipes.
Allow egg laying for 4‑5 days at room temperature.

steps.title: Transfer or discard parental D. virilis
steps.instruction: After egg laying, either move the parental D. virilis flies to a new food vial containing yeast granules or discard them in a morgue. Inspect each vial for larvae; if the medium is dry, add a few drops of distilled water. Discard any vial that contains fewer than 50 eggs or shows mold/fungal growth.

substeps.instruction: Transfer parental flies to a fresh vial with yeast granules or discard them.
Check vials for larvae; add distilled water if the medium is dry.
Discard vials with <50 eggs or visible mold/fungal contamination.

steps.title: Allow F1 pupation
steps.instruction: Let the F1 offspring develop and pupate at room temperature. Note that D. virilis requires 9‑10 days to complete its life cycle at 25 °C.

steps.title: Anesthetize CS flies for culture
steps.instruction: CO₂‑anesthetize Canton S (CS) wild‑type D. melanogaster flies that have been reared on standard medium in an incubator set to 25 °C, ~60 % relative humidity, and a 12:12 h light/dark cycle. Use flies that are 3‑15 days old and avoid those from overcrowded, mite‑infested, or fungus‑contaminated bottles.

steps.title: Separate male and female CS flies
steps.instruction: On a fly pad, separate the anesthetized CS flies into males and females.

steps.title: Set up CS parental bottle
steps.instruction: Place 25 female and 10 male CS flies into a bottle containing fresh standard medium. After the flies recover from anesthesia, move the bottle to the incubator. Ensure the bottle is free of condensed water before adding flies; after transfer, leave the bottle on its side for 1‑2 min until recovery.

substeps.instruction: Add 25 females and 10 males to a fresh medium bottle.
Confirm no condensed water is present; remove if necessary.
After recovery, place the bottle in the incubator.
Leave the bottle on its side for 1‑2 min to allow full recovery.

steps.title: Transfer or discard CS parental flies
steps.instruction: Three days after egg laying (when the eggs will become F1 flies), move the adult parental CS flies to a new bottle to continue the culture or discard them. Follow age‑dependent transfer schedules: if parents are 3‑5 days old, transfer to new bottles every 3 days for three transfers; if 6‑8 days old, transfer every 3 days for two transfers. Prefer younger parents (≤15 days). Inspect bottles for larval activity, discard any with poor egg‑lay, and add a few drops of distilled water if the medium is dry.

substeps.instruction: After 3 days, transfer parental flies to a fresh bottle or discard.
For 3‑5‑day‑old parents: transfer every 3 days for three rounds.
For 6‑8‑day‑old parents: transfer every 3 days for two rounds.
Prefer parents ≤15 days old.
Inspect for larval activity; discard poor‑laying bottles.
Add distilled water drops if the medium is dry.

steps.title: Maintain cultures until F1 emergence
steps.instruction: Continue incubating the bottles until the F1 CS adults emerge; these adults will be used for the egg‑laying assay.

steps.title: Record and analyze egg‑laying data
steps.instruction: Count the number of eggs laid each day (D1‑D5) for control and PP‑exposed groups. Use Microsoft Excel or GraphPad Prism to compute the average egg count, mean ± standard error of the mean (SEM) from at least three independent experiments, and the egg‑lay percentage (PP‑exposed mean divided by control mean for each day). Perform one‑way or two‑way ANOVA with Tukey, Bonferroni, or Dunnett’s correction for multiple comparisons to assess significance.

substeps.instruction: Count eggs laid on days D1‑D5 for each group.
Calculate average egg count and mean ± SEM (≥3 replicates).
Compute egg‑lay % = (PP‑exposed mean / control mean) × 100 for each day.
Run one‑way or two‑way ANOVA with appropriate post‑hoc correction.

steps.title: Calculate eclosion rate
steps.instruction: For the eclosion dataset, calculate percentage eclosion as (number of F1 progeny ÷ total mock F1 progeny) × 100. Exclude any vials where CS females died or escaped during transfer from the assay.

substeps.instruction: Compute eclosion % = (F1 progeny / mock F1 progeny) × 100.
Omit vials with dead CS females or escapees from analysis.
